newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Belgacom urges further privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Belgacom urges further privatisation.

text.p: Belgian telephone company Belgacom on Monday urged the Belgian state to sell its 50.1 stake in the operator and alleviate its hefty pension charges by injecting the capital gain on the sale in its Pension Fund.
"As management we are forced to look for a solution for the company's competitive handicaps," chief executive officer John Goossens told the daily Financieel Economische Tijd.
The rest of Belgacom's capital -- 49.9 percent -- is owned by a consortium including Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors.
The Wall Street Journal Europe said that senior management were urging the Belgian government to sell its stake through an initial public offering.
Belgacom or government officials were not immediately available for comment.
The Tijd said Belgacom paid 17 billion francs to the pension fund in 1996 for its 9,500 retired employees.

But the company will soon have to pay for an additional 5,000 people who are expected to accept an early retirement offer as part of a major restructuring programme which aims to cut the total workforce to 20,000.
The Tijd said the pension fund had 63 billion francs at the end of December 1996, but needed 160 billion francs according to international standards.
Goossens said politicians' attitude towards Belgacom had changed and that the state was now just involved in major decisions, which require a 75-percent majority of the votes.
"That's why it does not make much difference whether (the state) owns 50.1 percent or 25 percent in Belgacom," he said.
He said foreign examples showed that the state could even yield 99.9 percent without losing its grip on the most strategic decisions "on the one condition it acquires a 'golden' share".

Ameritech has repeatedly said it aimed to raise its stake in Belgacom and the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) advised the Belgian state last month to sell off its remaining interests in Belgacom.
